prompt.brief: Design a research-to-execution platform for reinforcement-learning trading agents that uses realistic backtests, strict risk controls, paper trading, and low-latency order execution.
successSignals: Define immutable market-data versions, point-in-time features, action/reward contracts, experiment lineage, and reproducible agent artifacts.
Model fees, slippage, latency, liquidity, partial fills, limits, market regimes, and leakage-resistant train/validation/test splits.
Separate offline training and simulation from a guarded paper/live execution path with idempotent orders and kill switches.
Explain risk limits, policy approval, drift, rollback, broker failure, auditability, observability, and safe degradation.

functional: Ingest and validate market data, build point-in-time datasets, train agents, run reproducible backtests, and compare risk-adjusted results.
Support paper trading and approved live execution with portfolio state, pre-trade risk checks, order status reconciliation, and kill switches.
Version policies and data, audit every decision/order, detect regime changes, and recover safely from broker or market-data outages.
nonFunctional: Keep execution decisions within the configured trading latency budget and require statistically robust, leakage-free evaluation before promotion.
Scale parallel training and backtests across many instruments without unbounded synchronous work or unsafe live rollout.
Do not lose committed state; make retries and duplicate events safe.
Degrade safely when downstream workers, caches, or external dependencies fail.
scaleAssumptions: Years of tick or bar data across thousands of instruments
Partition by the primary tenant, user, item, or geographic key and isolate hot partitions.
Keep serving state bounded; retain raw events or durable records for replay and auditing.

deepDives.title: Consistency and idempotency
points: Keep the Research-to-execution platform commit authoritative; let derived projections converge with visible version and freshness.
Use idempotency keys, conditional Research-to-execution platform writes, event IDs, and versions so retries and replay are safe.
Return Research-to-execution platform version and observedAt so clients can reason about freshness.

deepDives.title: Partitioning and hot keys
points: Partition Research-to-execution platform by its primary read and write keys, then isolate hot tenants, users, items, or regions.
Bound Research-to-execution platform work with backpressure and queue isolation so one hot key cannot dominate the cluster.
Keep a replay or reconciliation path for Research-to-execution platform projection drift and partial failures.

deepDives.title: Failure and recovery
points: Serve the last acceptable Research-to-execution platform projection or an explicit degraded response when workers fail.
Retain durable Research-to-execution platform records for replay and make each downstream effect independently retryable.
Measure Research-to-execution platform latency, backlog, freshness, error rate, and correctness drift.

tradeoffs.title: Strong consistency versus throughput
tradeoffs.recommendation: Strongly protect the business commit and use versioned eventual projections for high-volume reads.
tradeoffs.caution: Making every derived read synchronous increases coordination and tail latency.

tradeoffs.title: Push versus pull processing
tradeoffs.recommendation: Push bounded events to workers and pull durable snapshots on reads or recovery.
tradeoffs.caution: Unbounded fanout or full scans make bursts and hot keys expensive.

tradeoffs.title: Managed service versus custom control
tradeoffs.recommendation: Start with managed primitives where their limits match the access pattern, then isolate replaceable interfaces.
tradeoffs.caution: Provider defaults do not remove the need for quotas, replay, observability, and data lifecycle design.

commonMistakes: Putting all work on the synchronous request path.
Choosing a data store before writing the access patterns and consistency contract.
Ignoring retries, duplicate events, late data, deletion, privacy, or authorization.
Leaving hot partitions, backpressure, stale reads, and recovery unspecified.
Allowing unbounded requests or exports to compete with normal traffic.

followUps.question: What happens when the primary worker is unavailable?
followUps.answer: Acknowledge only after the durable boundary, serve the last acceptable projection, queue retryable work, and replay or reconcile after recovery.

followUps.question: How would you support a tenfold traffic spike?
followUps.answer: Pre-scale partitions, apply admission control and backpressure, isolate hot keys, cache immutable snapshots, and make freshness degradation visible.

followUps.question: How do you verify correctness?
followUps.answer: Use idempotency metrics, version gaps, sampled source-to-projection comparisons, replay tests, and a shadow rebuild before repair.
